name: AWS Lambda MicroVMs

modes.label: Arm64 (Graviton) baseline, us-east-1/us-east-2/us-west-2/ap-south-1
modes.note: Price List API Lambda-MicroVM-vCPU-Second-ARM $0.0000276944 = $0.0997/vCPU-h, Memory-GB-Second-ARM $0.0000036667 = $0.0132/GB-h. Baseline billed per second while running (2 GB : 1 vCPU; default 1 vCPU/2 GB, max baseline 4 vCPU/8 GB); automatic vertical burst up to 4x baseline (16 vCPU/32 GB) billed only while consumed. ap-south-1 matches us rates. Basis verified 2026-09-28: "You pay for baseline compute resources while your MicroVM is running. When your workload consumes resources above the baseline, you are charged only for the active duration of the additional memory and vCPU consumed." (https://aws.amazon.com/lambda/pricing/). Baseline = alloc; burst via burst_share knob. Idle: "After 5 minutes of inactivity, the MicroVM is automatically suspended based on the configured idle policy." (AWS launch blog).

plans.name: Pay-as-you-go
plans.note: Max lifetime configurable (example 28,800 s = 8 h). Auto-suspend after 5 min idle by default. Dedicated HTTPS endpoint per MicroVM.

knobs.label: Average burst above baseline (fraction of baseline)
knobs.why: Baseline-plus-consumption: resources used above the configured baseline (up to 4x) are billed per second on top; 0.5 = on average 50% extra above baseline. Engine rate multiplier = 1 + value.

caveats: All rates from the AWS Price List API (AWSLambda, publication 2026-09-19). Regions with MicroVM SKUs: us-east-1, us-east-2, us-west-2, eu-west-1, eu-north-1, eu-central-1, ap-south-1, ap-northeast-1, ap-southeast-1, ap-southeast-2.
The knob rate_factor for burst is an approximation: burst is billed only for seconds it is consumed, at the same unit rates (per pricing page "baseline-plus-consumption").

Snapshots (suspend = memory+disk): storage $0.0001111111/GB-h = $0.0811/GB-month; write $0.0037977/GB; read (on start/resume) $0.0015468/GB; MicroVM image storage has a 1-week minimum retention. Suspended VMs pay no compute.

Included disk size, minimum billed duration and any per-launch fee are not published. Running disk: the AWS Price List API (AWSLambda us-east-1, fetched 2026-09-28) has only vCPU, memory and snapshot storage/read/write SKUs for MicroVMs, no running-disk meter, so disk_gib_month = 0 (disk of a running MicroVM is not billed separately; it is billed as snapshot storage once suspended). Maximum disk size per MicroVM is unpublished. Whether Compute Savings Plans or the Lambda free tier apply is not stated (assumed no).
Max lifetime: the launch blog shows maximum-duration 28,800 s (8 h) as an example; the true cap is not stated.
Identical to the announced AgentCore Runtime v2 committed baseline rates ($0.0997/vCPU-h, $0.0132/GB-h).

Internet egress (AWS Price List API, AWSDataTransfer us-east-1, 2026-09): first 100 GB/month free aggregated across all services and regions, then $0.09/GB first 10 TB, $0.085 next 40 TB, $0.07 next 100 TB, $0.05 over 150 TB. eu-west-1 is also $0.09; ap-south-1 $0.1093; ap-northeast-1 $0.114; ap-southeast-1 $0.12 (first-10-TB tier). The engine uses the flat us-east-1 first tier.

VPC access via Lambda Network Connector; NAT gateway gotcha: tasks/functions in private subnets reach the internet through a NAT gateway at $0.045/h per gateway (~$32.85/month per AZ) plus $0.045/GB processed (us-east-1; eu-north-1 $0.046, ap-south-1 $0.056), charged ON TOP of the $0.09/GB egress. Not modelled; public IPv4 ($0.005/h) is the usual alternative.

fleet.verification: Personal details, email and phone; payment card may be required.
fleet.notes: New-account memory quota is explicitly reduced and unspecified. Published memory pool is 400 GB per region or 1,024 GB in us-east-1/us-west-2/us-east-2/ap-northeast-1, burstable to 4x; adjustable via Service Quotas. Machine count depends on configured RAM, not Lambda invocation concurrency.
